questions.stem: Increasing order of solubility of AgCl in (i) $\mathrm{H_2O}$, (ii) 1M NaCl (aq.), (iii) 1M $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$(aq.) and (iv) 1M $\mathrm{NaNO_3}$ (aq.) solution
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{H_2O}$ solubility $= \sqrt{K_{sp}}$
In 1M NaCl and in 1 M $\mathrm{CaCl_2}$ more the $[\mathrm{Cl^-}]$ less is the solubility
Hence $\mathrm{CaCl_2 < NaCl < H_2O < NaNO_3}$

questions.stem: An LPG (Liquified Petroleum Gas) cylinder weighs 15.0 kg when empty. When full, it weighs 30.0 kg and shows a pressure of 3.0 atm. In the course of usage at $27^\circ\mathrm{C}$, the mass of the full cylinder is reduced to 24.2 kg. The volume of the used gas in cubic metre at the normal usage condition (1 atm and $27^\circ\mathrm{C}$) is (assume LPG to be normal butane and it behaves ideally)
questions.solution:
Weight of gas = 15 kg
Weight of gas in the cylinder after use = 24.2 – 15.0 = 9.2
$\therefore$ Gas used = 15 – 9.2 = 5.8 kg
$\therefore V = \frac{w}{M} \times \frac{RT}{P} = \frac{5.8 \times 10^{3} \times 0.0821 \times 300}{58 \times 1}\ \mathrm{L}$
$= \frac{100 \times .0821 \times 300}{10^{3}}\ \mathrm{m^3}$
$= 2.463\ \mathrm{m^3}$

questions.stem: P and Q combines to form two compounds $\mathrm{PQ_2}$ and $\mathrm{PQ_3}$. If 1 g $\mathrm{PQ_2}$ is dissolved in 51 g benzene the depression of freezing point becomes $0.8^\circ\mathrm{C}$. On the other hand if 1 g $\mathrm{PQ_3}$ is dissolved in 51 g of benzene, the depression of freezing point becomes $0.625^\circ\mathrm{C}$. The atomic mass of P and Q are ($K_f$ of benzene $= 5.1\ \mathrm{K\,kg\,mol^{-1}}$)
questions.solution:
$0.8 = \frac{5.1 \times 1000 \times 1}{51 \times M_{PQ_2}} \Rightarrow M_{PQ_2} = 125$
$0.625 = \frac{5.1 \times 1000 \times 1}{51 \times M_{PQ_3}} \Rightarrow M_{PQ_3} = 160$
$\therefore$ At wt of P = 55 and Q = 35

questions.stem: For a chemical reaction, half-life period $\left(t_{\frac{1}{2}}\right)$ is 10 minutes. How much reactant will be left after 20 minutes if one starts with 100 moles of reactant and the order of the reaction be (i) zero, (ii) one and (iii) two?
questions.solution:
For zero order, $k = \frac{x}{t}$
$t_{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{a}{2K}$
$10 = \frac{100}{2 \times K} \Rightarrow K = 5$
$5 = \frac{x}{20} \Rightarrow x = 100\ \therefore (a - x) = 0$
For 1st order, No. of half lives $= \frac{20}{10} = 2$
$\therefore (a - x) = \frac{100}{2^{2}} = 25$
For 2nd order, $k = \frac{x}{at(a - x)}$
$\therefore t_{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{1}{ak}$
$10 = \frac{1}{100 \times k} \Rightarrow k = 10^{-3}$
$\therefore 10^{-3} = \frac{x}{100 \times 20 \times (100 - x)}$
$\Rightarrow x = 66.66$
$\therefore (a - x) = 33.33$

questions.stem: Equal volume of two solutions A and B of a strong acid having pH = 6.0 and pH = 4.0 respectively are mixed together to form a new solution. The pH of the new solution will be in the range
questions.solution:
pH = 6 $\quad \therefore [\mathrm{H^+}] = 10^{-6}\ \mathrm{M}$
Let volume is 1L
1L $10^{-6}$M SA contains $10^{-6}$ moles $\mathrm{H^+}$
pH = 4 $\quad \therefore [\mathrm{H^+}] = 10^{-4}\ \mathrm{M}$
1L $10^{-4}$ M SA contains $10^{-4}$ moles $\mathrm{H^+}$
$\therefore$ Total $\mathrm{H^+} = 10^{-6} + 10^{-4} = 1.01 \times 10^{-4}$ moles
$\therefore \left[\mathrm{H^+}\right] = \frac{1.01 \times 10^{-4}}{2}(\mathrm{M}) = 5.05 \times 10^{-5}$
pH $= -\log(5.05 \times 10^{-5}) = 4.29$

questions.stem: Adiabatic free expansion of ideal gas must be
questions.solution:
According to first law of thermodynamics
$Q = dU - W$
$\Rightarrow Q = dU - \left[-P_{external}\left(V_f - V_i\right)\right]$
[In Adiabatic Process Q = 0, In Free expansion $P_{external} = 0$]
$\therefore$ Putting the values, we get $\Rightarrow dU = 0\ \therefore U$ = constant
As internal energy remains unchanged; temperature must be constant.
$\therefore$ Isothermal Process

questions.stem: In the following reaction, the major product (H) is
Which of the following hydrogen bonds is likely to be the weakest?
questions.solution:
For $x - \overset{\delta+}{\mathrm{H}} \cdots \overset{\delta-}{\mathrm{O}}$ hydrogen bond; lower the electronegativity of x; lower is the residual $\delta+$ change induced on H & hence a lesser electrostatic attraction is expected between H & O; thus diminishing bond strength.
Hence, chosen option is the atom of lowest electronegativity, i.e. C.

questions.stem: How many oxygen atoms are present in 0.36 g of a drop of water at STP?
questions.solution:
0.36 g water drop has $\frac{0.36}{18}$ moles
$\frac{0.36}{18}$ moles of water has $\frac{0.36}{18} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23}$ molecules of water
1 molecule of water has 1 oxygen atom.
$\therefore$ Number of O atoms $= \frac{0.36}{18} \times 6.023 \times 10^{23} = 1.205 \times 10^{22}$

questions.stem: 360 $\mathrm{cm^3}$ of a hydrocabon diffuses in 30 minutes, while under the same conditions 360 $\mathrm{cm^3}$ of $\mathrm{SO_2}$ gas diffuses in one hour. The molecular formula of the hydrocabon is
questions.solution:
According to Graham’s Law: (MW = Molecular Weight)
$\frac{R_d(\text{hydrocarbon})}{R_d(\mathrm{SO_2})} = \sqrt{\frac{MW_{\mathrm{SO_2}}}{MW_{\text{hydrocarbon}}}}$
$\Rightarrow \frac{360/30}{360/60} = \sqrt{\frac{64}{MW_{\text{hydrocarbon}}}}$
$\Rightarrow 4 = \frac{64}{MW_{\text{hydrocabon}}}$
$\Rightarrow MW_{\text{hydrocarbon}} = \frac{64}{4} = 16$
$\mathrm{CH_4}$ is the hydrocarbon with possible molecular weight 16.

questions.stem: The molar conductances of $\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}$, $\mathrm{BaCl_2}$ and $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ at infinite dilution are 523.28, 280.0 and 129.8 $\mathrm{S\,cm^2\,mol^{-1}}$ respectively. The molar conductance of $\mathrm{NH_4OH}$ at infinite dilution will be
questions.solution:
$2\lambda^{\infty}_{m[\mathrm{NH_4OH}]} = 2\lambda^{\infty}_{m[\mathrm{NH_4Cl}]} - \lambda^{\infty}_{m[\mathrm{BaCl_2}]} + \lambda^{\infty}_{m[\mathrm{Ba(OH)_2}]}$
$2\lambda^{\infty}_{m(\mathrm{NH_4OH})} = 2 \times (129.8) - 280 + 523.28$
$2\lambda^{\infty}_{m(\mathrm{NH_4OH})} = 502.88$
$\lambda^{\infty}_{m(\mathrm{NH_4OH})} = 251.44\ \mathrm{S\,cm^2\,mol^{-1}}$

questions.stem: The number of terminal and bridging hydrogens in $\mathrm{B_2H_6}$ are respectively

Consider the following gas phase dissociation, $\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}$ with equilibrium constant $K_P$ at a particular temperature and at pressure P. The degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) for $\mathrm{PCl_5(g)}$ is
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{PCl_5(g) \rightleftharpoons PCl_3(g) + Cl_2(g)}$
initially moles taken | 1 | 0 | 0
moles of equilibrium | $1 - \alpha$ | $\alpha$ | $\alpha$
$K_P = \frac{P_{\mathrm{PCl_3}} \cdot P_{\mathrm{Cl_2}}}{P_{\mathrm{PCl_5}}} \qquad \because P = X_{gas} \cdot P_T$
$K_P = \frac{\left(\frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P\right)^{2}}{\left(\frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha} \cdot P\right)} \qquad X_{\mathrm{PCl_3}} = X_{\mathrm{Cl_2}} = \frac{\alpha}{1+\alpha}$
$K_P = \frac{\alpha^{2}P}{1 - \alpha^{2}} \qquad X_{\mathrm{PCl_5}} = \frac{1-\alpha}{1+\alpha}$
$\alpha = \left(\frac{K_P}{K_P + P}\right)^{1/2}$

questions.stem:
As per the following equation, 0.217g of HgO (molecular mass = $217\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}$) reacts with excess iodide. On titration of the resulting solution, how many mL of 0.01 M HCl is required to reach the equivalence point?
$\mathrm{HgO + 4I^- + H_2O \longrightarrow HgI_4^{2-} + 2OH^-}$
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{HgO + 4I^- + H_2O \rightarrow HgI_4^{-2} + 2OH^-}$
(limiting reagent) (excess reagent)
$\mathrm{2H^+ (HC\ell) + 2OH^- \rightarrow 2H_2O(\ell)}$
$\therefore n_{\mathrm{HgO}} = \frac{1}{2}n_{\mathrm{H^+}} = \frac{1}{2}n_{\mathrm{HC\ell}}$
$\frac{0.217}{217} = \frac{1}{2} \times M \times \frac{V(\mathrm{mL})}{1000} = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.01 \times \frac{V(\mathrm{mL})}{1000}$
$\therefore V(\mathrm{mL}) = 200$

questions.stem: An egg takes 4.0 minutes to boil at sea level where the boiling point of water is $T_1$K, where as it takes 8.0 minutes to boil on a mountain top where the boiling point of water is $T_2$K. The activation energy for the reaction that takes place during the boiling of egg is
questions.solution:
As per Arrhenius Equation
$\ln\left(\frac{K_2}{K_1}\right) = \frac{E_a}{R}\left[\frac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1T_2}\right]$
According to question
$\ln\left(\frac{1/8}{1/4}\right) = \frac{E_a}{R}\left[\frac{T_1 - T_2}{T_1T_2}\right]$
$\ln 2 = \frac{E_a}{R}\left[\frac{T_1 - T_2}{T_1T_2}\right]$
$0.693 = \frac{E_a}{R}\left[\frac{T_1 - T_2}{T_1T_2}\right]$
$\therefore E_a = 0.693R\frac{T_1T_2}{T_1 - T_2}$
